record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Consider two Lagrangian fibrations phi: M 4 → B and phi′: M ′4 → B′. Assume that B and B′ are affinely equivalent in the sense that there exists an affine d iffeomorphism psi: B → B′. Is it true that under these assumptions the corresponding Lagr angian fibrations are symplectomorphic? In the local and semi-global setting, we may ask a similar question for a Lagrangian fibration in a neigh- bourhood of a singular point or of a singular fiber. According to the E liasson theorem [72, 166, 169], in the non-degenerate case, there are no local symplectic invarian ts. In other words, non-degenerate singular points of the same topological (algebraic) type are locally fib erwise symplectomorphic. The case of non-degenerate singular fibers has been discussed in [65, 2 25, 185, 186] for basic singularities of elliptic, hyperbolic, and focus types. One of the main observation s made in these papers is that every action variable can be written in the form I = Ising + Ireg, where the singular part Ising is the same for all singularities of a given topological type (due to Eliasson's result) and Ireg is a smooth function which can be arbitrary. This regular part (or its Taylor exp ansion) in many cases may serve as a complete symplectic invariant in semi-global setting. Let us now discuss what happens in the case of degenerate singular ities.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\phi: M^4 \to B$ and $\phi': M'^4 \to B'$ be two Lagrangian fibrations of four-dimensional symplectic manifolds (so each fiber is a smooth Lagrangian submanifold). The bases $B$ and $B'$ carry the natural integral affine structures induced by action variables (away from singular values). Assume that $B$ and $B'$ are affinely equivalent, i.e., there exists an affine diffeomorphism $\psi: B \to B'$ that preserves the integral affine structure (and, in the singular setting, the stratification by singular values together with the topological types of singularities).

Question: Does there necessarily exist a fiberwise symplectomorphism $\Phi: M \to M'$ covering $\psi$, that is, with $\phi' \circ \Phi = \psi \circ \phi$?

Formulate and answer the same question in the following local and semi-global settings:
(a) globally, for $\phi$ and $\phi'$ defined on all of $M^4$ and $M'^4$;
(b) locally, in a neighborhood of a singular point of the fibration;
(c) semi-globally, in a saturated neighborhood of a singular fiber.

In particular, determine whether affine equivalence of the bases is a complete symplectic invariant of the Lagrangian fibration in each of the settings (a), (b), and (c), including the case of degenerate singularities.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a 2018 survey of finite-dimensional integrable systems. Subsequent work (e.g., on symplectic invariants for parabolic orbits and cusp singularities, and on hypersemitoric systems) addresses particular non-degenerate and some degenerate singular cases via the "I_sing + I_reg" decomposition, but no general affirmative or negative answer in the global or degenerate semi-global setting appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems, Questions, and Challenges in Finite-Dimensional Integrable Systems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys open problems in finite-dimensional integrable systems, including Problem 2.2 on whether affine equivalence of bases implies symplectomorphism of Lagrangian fibrations.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Symplectic invariants for parabolic orbits and cusp singularities of integrable systems
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs semi-global symplectic invariants for specific degenerate singularities (parabolic orbits, cusps) of integrable Hamiltonian systems.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress in the semi-global degenerate setting, but no general resolution.

status_evidence.title: Towards hypersemitoric systems
status_evidence.snippet: Develops symplectic classification theory in semitoric/hypersemitoric settings, extending Delzant-type results.
status_evidence.claim: Recent extensions of the symplectic classification of Lagrangian fibrations, leaving the general problem open.
